source_text: Iniquitas iniqui - inquit - super caput eius; unumquemque vestrum secundum vias suas iudicabo [n73] . Non morientur patres pro filiis neque filii pro parentibus; anima - inquit - quae peccat, ipsa morietur; quoniam omnes animae meae sunt, unumquemque pro suis iniquitatibus iudicabo [n74] .
pass_a_gloss: The iniquity of the iniquitous, he says, upon his head; I will judge each of you according to your ways. Fathers shall not die for sons nor sons for parents; the soul, he says, which sins, itself will die; since all souls are mine, I will judge each one for his own iniquities.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS anima; Blaise human soul as image

pass_b_english: ‘The wicked person’s iniquity,’ he says, ‘is upon his own head. I will judge each of you according to your own ways’ (Ezekiel 18:20, 30). ‘Fathers shall not die for their children, nor children for their parents’ (Deuteronomy 24:16). ‘The soul that sins shall itself die. All souls are mine; I will judge each person for that person’s own iniquities’ (Ezekiel 18:4, 30).

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Scripture's destruction of iniquitas is the Law's purpose; keep moral injustice.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.
